# AP-8: eight primes in arithmetic progression, 1060 digits

> **Older record (27 Nov 2026):** this AP-8 was on the Prime Pages AP-8 list until 6 November 2026, when four 1,101-digit AP-8s by the same discoverer passed it ([`ap8-1101-1/`](../../ap8-1101-1/) to [`ap8-1101-4/`](../../ap8-1101-4/)).

```
(1950740727977 + 445136050·n)·2459# + 1,   n = 0, 1, ..., 7
```

Eight primes in arithmetic progression, each with 1060 digits. Here 2459# is the product of all primes up to 2459
(the primorial). The common difference is 445136050·2459#.

- **Found:** 4 November 2026
- **Discoverer:** Arnav Garg ([arnavgarg.in](https://arnavgarg.in))
- **Proof:** all eight terms are proven prime. Each has an ECPP certificate in the format of [CM](https://www.multiprecision.org/cm/) by
  Andreas Enge, checked with its `ecpp-check` verifier, and an N−1 certificate.
- The terms for n = −1 and n = 8 are composite, so the progression has exactly eight terms.

Not a record. On 5 November 2026 this progression was #4 on the Prime Pages [AP-8 Top 20 list](https://t5k.org/top20/page.php?id=14). It dropped off that list on 6 November 2026, when the four 1,101-digit AP-8s in this repository were listed.

## Files

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `terms.txt` | all eight terms in decimal |
| `certificates/t<n>.ecpp.cert` | ECPP certificate of term n (CM format) |
| `certificates/t<n>.nminus1.txt` | N−1 certificate of term n: N, the factored part of N−1 and the witnesses |
| `certificates.zip` | the same 16 certificate files in one archive |
| `record.json` | the numbers above, for scripts |

## Checking it yourself

Probable-prime check of all terms, and that they form the progression (Python with gmpy2):

```python
import gmpy2
a, d, p = 1950740727977, 445136050, gmpy2.primorial(2459)
terms = [(a + d * n) * p + 1 for n in range(8)]
assert all(gmpy2.is_prime(t) for t in terms)
assert all(len(str(t)) == 1060 for t in terms)
assert not gmpy2.is_prime((a - d) * p + 1) and not gmpy2.is_prime((a + 8 * d) * p + 1)
print("8 terms, 1060 digits each, probable primes")
```

Proofs, with CM installed:

```
for n in $(seq 0 7); do ecpp-check -f certificates/t$n.ecpp.cert; done
```

Each run should print that the file contains a valid ECPP certificate in the CM format. The first number in each
certificate is the term it proves.
